stem: Which sentence from “No Dream Is Impossible” connects most closely to a central idea from “A History of Fearlessness”?

options.label: A
options.text: That part of me seemed to know that no matter how difficult achieving my goal might be, or even if I never achieved it, I would be happier striving toward my dream than if I tried to find security in a life I was unsuited for.

options.label: B
options.text: The voice seems very stern at times, as it makes me accept the responsibility for my failures and shortcomings, instead of excusing them or laying the blame elsewhere.

options.label: C
options.text: This time it had a new message: “Look at yourself honestly.”

options.label: D
options.text: After I recovered from the first shock of this discovery, to my surprise I began to feel stronger and more hopeful about the future.
